sUSD: existing pool connections and issuer-specific bridge
minting
The subsequent integration and wallet audit (Appendix 69) verifies five historical local DAI-wrapper
mints by e121 and the wider integration catalogue. The relay audit (Appendix 46) verifies inherited
Optimism withdrawals settled after the fork. Fresh private-L2 synth issuance and messaging remain
unverified.
1 October 2026. Read-only extension of the integrated network study (Appendix 37). No mint, burn,
relay, administrative action or state-changing simulation was executed.
The later control and storage audit (Appendix 67) confirms the copied seven-day finality setting,
compares Safe signers/modules/implementations to inherited state, and identifies the local DAI/sUSD
wrapper with reopened capacity. Its later findings govern those questions; the earlier checkpoint
evidence below retains its original scope.
What was already covered, and what this pass adds
sUSD was included as a Synthetix monetary family, a candidate collateral/debt supply route and an
accepted input in the sampled mStable mUSD basket. It had not received a dedicated audit of its synth
bridge. This pass identifies its six inherited Curve connections and checks the copied Synthetix bridge/
resolver configuration separately from the pARB escrow gateway.
The destination identity criterion is straightforward: the token ultimately delivered to PulseChain
must be the existing token accepted by the intended pool or issuer. L2 and L1 addresses need
not match. Minting on PulseChain is one way to obtain that token; releasing escrow or delivering existing
inventory are others. A new bridged wrapper must first be converted into an accepted token or become
explicitly supported collateral/pool inventory.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 422

Existing L1 connections

at Ethereum block 17,232,999, the verified matching PulseChain inherited boundary of 10 May 2023,
returns the following six connections. This is pool membership, not measured current usable balances or
trade capacity.

The sampled mUSD basket also accepts this existing local sUSD alongside USDC, DAI and USDT, subject
to its weight limits and working issuance. That adds a candidate path from sUSD to mUSD and then
mUSD/3CRV. It does not make mUSD exclusively sUSD-backed or remove other basket constraints. See
the issuer implementation and quote audit (Appendix 38).
                                        ┌─ four-coin pool ─ pDAI / pUSDC / pUSDT
                                        ├─ sUSD/3CRV ───── 3pool underlying
Existing PulseChain sUSD ────────────────┼─ sUSD/FRAXBP ─── FRAX / pUSDC
                                        ├─ eligible Aave conversion ─ DAI/sUSD route
                                        └─ accepted mUSD basket ─ mUSD/3CRV
These are candidate conversions with separately available liquidity and issuance limits. The Aave route
must use eligible receipts/underlying interfaces; it is not an oracle-driven automatic exchange.
Two different bridge paths
pARB standard gateway: escrow return
At the earlier integrated-network checkpoint, PulseChain block 27,681,116, the pARB router returns
standard gateway 0xa3a7b6f88361f48403514059f1f16c8e78d60eec for sUSD. That gateway calculates L2
counterpart 0xa970af1a584579b618be4d69ad6f73459d112f95. A source deployment at that calculated address was
not verified. The gateway's selected local sUSD balance was zero.
The saved standard gateway implementation releases escrow. This branch can return the existing local
sUSD token when properly funded and authenticated; its calculated mapping does not confer fresh sUSD
mint rights. It should not be confused with the Synthetix-specific bridge below.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 423

Synthetix synth bridge: authenticated issuer minting
Synthetix's historical SIP-229, marked implemented, describes burning a synth on one layer and minting
it through the Issuer on the other after authenticated cross-chain messaging. It initially enables sUSD
and concerns Ethereum/Optimism. That is an existing issuer-specific architecture closely aligned with the
proposed direct-L1-output route, rather than a generic escrow release.
Fresh destination getters are fixed at PulseChain chain 369, block 27,683,120, hash 
0x9c1323a0bf94a1d0f38684c98891a7cad2f33fd09c45ca5aca16db76a2cd916c. They establish:

The unprefixed resolver key SynthetixBridgeToBase returns zero; the bridge source actually uses the
prefixed ovm:SynthetixBridgeToBase key, whose getter succeeds. A zero result for an incorrect key must not
be interpreted as absence of the configured counterpart.
The verified copied SynthetixBridgeT oOptimism source contains finalizeSynthTransfer. It requires the caller
to be its messenger and the messenger's cross-domain sender to be its configured counterpart. The
function updates its received-transfer accounting and calls the Issuer's issueSynthsWithoutDebt(currencyKey,
destination, amount). That method name describes the destination issuance operation; it does not mean
the consolidated source debt/backing disappears.
The verified synth implementation is MultiCollateralSynth. Its issue/burn functions restrict callers to
authorized internal contracts and update token-state balances and supply. The new reads confirm that
the Issuer's sUSD mapping identifies this exact implementation, not an arbitrary newly deployed
wrapper.
The sampled Issuer explorer response contains no verified source body. Full Issuer authorization, debt-
accounting dependencies, copied messenger finality/authentication, source-chain operation and
complete end-to-end transfer execution remain unresolved. The enabled setting and unsuspended
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 424

destination are useful local predicates; they do not prove a live funded cross-chain route. Upstream
architecture and verified bridge source are stronger evidence than a name or deterministic counterpart
calculation, but they are not a successful transfer receipt.
What this means for the pDAI thesis
sUSD is a useful additional network junction because its existing address reaches both major Curve
bases, the direct four-coin pool and mUSD's collateral basket. If an authorized source/bridge/Issuer path
creates or delivers that existing sUSD, ordinary permitted trades could use those connections without
changing their coin lists. Correct pool output identity is the essential integration condition.
There are three candidate ways to supply it: acquire existing local sUSD; mint through Synthetix's valid
local collateral/debt mechanism; or use an authenticated issuer-specific synth transfer. The native synth
transfer design uses the copied Optimism messenger/counterpart, while the earlier escrow mapping
belongs to pARB. A pARB assertion or arbitrary L2 mint is not automatically accepted by the Optimism
messenger or authorized Synthetix Issuer. A compatible source environment or properly authorized
integration remains necessary.
Unlike OUSD's eligible-holder yield rebase or DOLA's Fed venue-management design, sUSD's ordinary
synth supply changes through permitted issuance/burning and debt/transfer accounting. Adding sUSD to
a Curve pool does not automatically expand or contract its balance to restore $1. The useful supply
buffer is the functioning authorized issuance/retirement route plus inventory management.
For example, supplying existing sUSD to a funded Curve exchange could acquire cheap pDAI.
Conversely, accumulated pDAI could buy discounted sUSD for debt retirement or another eligible
conversion. This could support both local markets when directions, fees, available inventory and
obligations are accounted for. Continuously selling newly supplied sUSD can consume the pool's pStables
and weaken sUSD's own quote; the broader controller still needs a return and contraction policy.
The synth's inherited/current token-owner comparison matches the same 0xeb31…7769 address. Fresh
Issuer/bridge owner getters also identify that address. These are contract authority observations, not
proof that the proposed group controls it or that Synthetix governance was taken over. Current upstream
reforms are not automatically installed on the copied chain; this study evaluates the copied contracts
and records the historical architecture separately.
The source-side financing loop
The proposed mechanism closely matches a documented Synthetix route. SCCP-264, created 16
December 2022 and marked implemented, specifies Ethereum/Optimism DAI wrappers whose output is
sUSD. SCCP-2011, created 26 May 2023 and marked implemented, explicitly describes starting with DAI
on Optimism, minting sUSD in the wrapper, bridging it to Ethereum, and burning for DAI or selling where
sUSD trades at a premium. Its parameter changes are later than the inherited 10 May boundary and
must not be imported into PulseChain without checking the copied deployment.
The relevant input operation is deposit accepted collateral into an authorized synth wrapper,
rather than generic staking in a pool. SIP-182 describes a factory that supports approved ERC20/synth
pairs, with per-wrapper maximum token amounts and mint/burn fees. Classic SNX staking issues debt
against SNX. V3 collateral delegation and spot wrappers have different accounting and outputs. LP
deposits into Curve alone acquire LP shares and do not authorize synth issuance.
The already-saved verified MultiCollateralSynth implementation has a material additional authorization
branch: its _isInternalContract override accepts registered CollateralManager contracts, factory-
recognized wrappers and the EtherWrapper, as well as its base internal contracts. This establishes that
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 425

the inherited destination synth design supports recognized collateral wrappers. It does not identify an
operational pARB wrapper, accepted pARB collateral address, available cap or source oracle. No new
state-changing call was used to examine it.
Proposed pARB source                                      PulseChain destination
Accepted asserted pStable
         │
         │ authorized wrapper / valid collateral issuance
         │ [source deployment, asset and capacity unverified]
         ▼
Source synth ── burn ── authenticated message + finality ── mint existing sUSD
                       [pARB integration unverified]          │
                       [copied Optimism bridge inspected]     ├─ direct pool → pDAI/pUSDC/pUSDT
                                                             ├─ 3CRV → other metapools
                                                             ├─ FRAXBP → other metapools
                                                             └─ accepted basket → local mUSD
An assertion accepted by a rollup establishes state/message acceptance under that rollup's rules. It is
not by itself permission to mint any ERC20. Even assuming spendable pStable balances exist on pARB, a
wrapper must accept their exact source token address, value them under its own rules and have
issuance capacity. The resulting synth must also have a valid route to the destination bridge. The copied
bridge authenticates its configured Optimism messenger/counterpart. An unrelated pARB gateway or
validator assertion does not satisfy that check automatically.
The Arbitrum version distinction
SIP-367, created 12 March 2024 and marked implemented, describes Synthetix V3 on Arbitrum:
collateral-backed issuance of an Arbitrum-native stablecoin, proposed name USDh, and separate USDC/
sUSDC and DAI/sDAI spot wrappers. Its configured issuance ratios and caps are not evidence for the
copied V2 sUSD system. The later SCCP-336 describes changing Arbitrum's collateral set and disabling
its DAI wrapper, further illustrating that accepted assets are configuration-dependent.
Therefore, “Synthetix exists on Arbitrum” is not enough to prove the desired bridge output. If a pARB
installation uses V3, its output needs a verified interconversion or authorized transfer integration that
ends in existing PulseChain sUSD. If it instead deploys a compatible V2 source, its wrapper and accepted
messenger still need to be identified. Neither source installation has been established by this research.
How the connected assets are reached
The inherited pool catalogue establishes these local market connections:
Connection What it permits in principle What must be checked separately

local base stables

and trade size

the base stables
Swap/deposit/withdraw interfaces,
distinct pool inventory
sUSD / FRAXBP and eUSD / FRAXBP Route through the shared FRAX/USDC
base
Usable reserves; Reserve issuer
collateral acceptance if minting eUSD

MIM / 3CRV, MIM / FRAXBP and sUSD /
UST / MIM
Several market paths to MIM Existing MIM supply/liquidity; legacy
UST is not sound dollar backing by
assumption
V2 aDAI / aSUSD A lending-receipt path between local
DAI and sUSD
Aave V2 deposit/redemption and pool-
specific interfaces; not V3 Portal aDAI

mUSD from eligible sUSD
Weight limits, fees, collateral status
and complete mint success
The exact OUSD/3CRV pool is 0x87650d7bbfc3a9f10587d7778206671719d9910d; the sampled Reserve eUSD/
FRAXBP pool is 0xaeda92e6a3b1028edc139a4ae56ec881f3064d4f. MIM/3CRV is 
0x5a6a4d54456819380173272a5e8e9b9904bdf41b and MIM/FRAXBP is 0xb3bc1833ac51aacea92acd551fbe1ab7edc59edf.
Catalogue entries are preserved in the financing batch alongside their source catalogue reference.
The aDAI receipt in the sUSD/Aave pool is V2 0x028171bca77440897b824ca71d1c56cac55b68a3; its aSUSD
counterpart is 0x6c5024cd4f8a59110119c56f8933403a539555eb. V3 aDAI 0x018008bfb33d285247a21d44e50697654f754e63
belongs to a different route. Identifying both as “aDAI” would falsely merge the two systems.
A shared base is a market connection, not direct issuer backing. Buying OUSD or eUSD through their
metapools is distinct from minting them. OUSD's sampled issuer accepts DAI/USDC/USDT; Reserve eUSD
requires its eligible collateral basket; MIM requires its own authorized issuance route. The system could
nevertheless use sUSD to reach their existing markets without first minting each issuer's stablecoin or
changing each Curve coin list. This makes sUSD a potentially simpler first distribution route than
separately installing many bridged wrappers.
Timing, scale and the return route
Synthetix's 1 March 2023 announcement confirms the original native Optimism-to-Ethereum sUSD
transfer had a seven-day wait. It distinguishes that native transfer from a faster aggregator alternative.
The copied PulseChain route's actual challenge/finality period, relaying and source operation remain
unverified. A liquidity provider can front destination tokens sooner only if it has inventory and accepts
the settlement risk; it does not remove native settlement.
For purchases every ten seconds, a seven-day replenishment interval contains 60,480 purchase
opportunities. If each purchase spends q sUSD, the corresponding flow consumes 60,480 × q sUSD. A
1,000-sUSD purchase uses 60.48 million sUSD across the interval, before gas, fees, delays and
additional reserves. This is a working-inventory illustration, not a measured capacity estimate. A large
initial bridge transfer can settle first and fund gradual purchases later; 50 billion tokens need not enter
an LP together. Issuance volume, bridging volume, swap size and LP inventory are four different controls.
The controller also needs the reverse operation. It can acquire pDAI when cheap, then later use
inventory to buy discounted sUSD, retire source synth obligations or redeem eligible collateral. Source
wrappers can provide a mint/burn supply buffer within their capacity and custody rules. Minting more
sUSD and selling it repeatedly without a return flow fills destination pools with sUSD and removes their
counter-assets. This supports pDAI temporarily while potentially weakening sUSD. Multiple metapools
sharing 3CRV or FRAXBP do not multiply the same underlying reserves.
For a collateral wrapper, the synth claim is linked to deposited collateral and its accepted redemption
route; its accounting is not identical to a new SNX staker loan. For the native transfer, source burning
and destination minting relocate the claim; they do not duplicate it or create external dollar backing.
T oken balances, source collateral, in-transit amounts and obligations must each be counted once. The
absence of a new destination SNX debt allocation is not the absence of a system-wide claim.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 427

The thesis can therefore state: a verified collateral-to-synth source and authenticated existing-
token bridge could turn L2 balances into usable L1 Curve inventory. The upstream Optimism
precedent and the inspected destination bridge support that architecture. The complete pARB instance
remains contingent on identified source collateral acceptance, compatible synth output, accepted
messaging and working finality, followed by measured destination liquidity. Evidence for these specific
connections would resolve the present uncertainty; further token names or governance assumptions
would not.
Reproduction
Raw getter/source records are preserved under artifacts/pulsechain-susd-route-20261001/. Explicit getter-
only manifests are Research/experiments/pulsechain_susd_{proxy,implementation,resolver,controls,bridge_path}
_20261001.json. Use Research/scripts/probe_pulsechain_routes.py --calls with a retaining RPC and the recorded
block for reproduction. Source responses are stored unchanged, including the unverified Issuer response.
Hashes and selected older pool/bridge inputs appear in the batch manifest. Production and research
code were not changed; the previous 63-test/82-subtest result remains the last code-validation result
and was not rerun for this documentation/getter extension.
The financing extension uses explicit batch artifacts/pulsechain-susd-financing-20261001/ and manifest 
Research/experiments/pulsechain_susd_financing_20261001.json. It saves eight primary-source documents, the
Synthetix SIP repository commit, hashes, connected pool rows and the earlier archive hashes. It makes
no new blockchain calls. The historical timing calculation uses only 604,800 seconds divided by a ten-
second interval; it is not evidence of a seven-day PulseChain delay or a funded 60.48-million-sUSD route.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 428

Unlike OUSD's eligible-holder yield rebase or DOLA's Fed venue-management design, sUSD's ordinary
synth supply changes through permitted issuance/burning and debt/transfer accounting. Adding sUSD to
a Curve pool does not automatically expand or contract its balance to restore $1. The useful supply
buffer is the functioning authorized issuance/retirement route plus inventory management.
For example, supplying existing sUSD to a funded Curve exchange could acquire cheap pDAI.
Conversely, accumulated pDAI could buy discounted sUSD for debt retirement or another eligible
conversion. This could support both local markets when directions, fees, available inventory and
obligations are accounted for. Continuously selling newly supplied sUSD can consume the pool's pStables
and weaken sUSD's own quote; the broader controller still needs a return and contraction policy.
The synth's inherited/current token-owner comparison matches the same 0xeb31…7769 address. Fresh
Issuer/bridge owner getters also identify that address. These are contract authority observations, not
proof that the proposed group controls it or that Synthetix governance was taken over. Current upstream
reforms are not automatically installed on the copied chain; this study evaluates the copied contracts
and records the historical architecture separately.
The source-side financing loop
The proposed mechanism closely matches a documented Synthetix route. SCCP-264, created 16
December 2022 and marked implemented, specifies Ethereum/Optimism DAI wrappers whose output is
sUSD. SCCP-2011, created 26 May 2023 and marked implemented, explicitly describes starting with DAI
on Optimism, minting sUSD in the wrapper, bridging it to Ethereum, and burning for DAI or selling where
sUSD trades at a premium. Its parameter changes are later than the inherited 10 May boundary and
must not be imported into PulseChain without checking the copied deployment.
The relevant input operation is deposit accepted collateral into an authorized synth wrapper,
rather than generic staking in a pool. SIP-182 describes a factory that supports approved ERC20/synth
pairs, with per-wrapper maximum token amounts and mint/burn fees. Classic SNX staking issues debt
against SNX. V3 collateral delegation and spot wrappers have different accounting and outputs. LP
deposits into Curve alone acquire LP shares and do not authorize synth issuance.

The Arbitrum version distinction
SIP-367, created 12 March 2024 and marked implemented, describes Synthetix V3 on Arbitrum:
collateral-backed issuance of an Arbitrum-native stablecoin, proposed name USDh, and separate USDC/
sUSDC and DAI/sDAI spot wrappers. Its configured issuance ratios and caps are not evidence for the
copied V2 sUSD system. The later SCCP-336 describes changing Arbitrum's collateral set and disabling
its DAI wrapper, further illustrating that accepted assets are configuration-dependent.
Therefore, “Synthetix exists on Arbitrum” is not enough to prove the desired bridge output. If a pARB
installation uses V3, its output needs a verified interconversion or authorized transfer integration that
ends in existing PulseChain sUSD. If it instead deploys a compatible V2 source, its wrapper and accepted
messenger still need to be identified. Neither source installation has been established by this research.

Timing, scale and the return route
Synthetix's 1 March 2023 announcement confirms the original native Optimism-to-Ethereum sUSD
transfer had a seven-day wait. It distinguishes that native transfer from a faster aggregator alternative.
The copied PulseChain route's actual challenge/finality period, relaying and source operation remain
unverified. A liquidity provider can front destination tokens sooner only if it has inventory and accepts
the settlement risk; it does not remove native settlement.
For purchases every ten seconds, a seven-day replenishment interval contains 60,480 purchase
opportunities. If each purchase spends q sUSD, the corresponding flow consumes 60,480 × q sUSD. A
1,000-sUSD purchase uses 60.48 million sUSD across the interval, before gas, fees, delays and
additional reserves. This is a working-inventory illustration, not a measured capacity estimate. A large
initial bridge transfer can settle first and fund gradual purchases later; 50 billion tokens need not enter
an LP together. Issuance volume, bridging volume, swap size and LP inventory are four different controls.
The controller also needs the reverse operation. It can acquire pDAI when cheap, then later use
inventory to buy discounted sUSD, retire source synth obligations or redeem eligible collateral. Source
wrappers can provide a mint/burn supply buffer within their capacity and custody rules. Minting more
sUSD and selling it repeatedly without a return flow fills destination pools with sUSD and removes their
counter-assets. This supports pDAI temporarily while potentially weakening sUSD. Multiple metapools
sharing 3CRV or FRAXBP do not multiply the same underlying reserves.
For a collateral wrapper, the synth claim is linked to deposited collateral and its accepted redemption
route; its accounting is not identical to a new SNX staker loan. For the native transfer, source burning
and destination minting relocate the claim; they do not duplicate it or create external dollar backing.
T oken balances, source collateral, in-transit amounts and obligations must each be counted once. The
absence of a new destination SNX debt allocation is not the absence of a system-wide claim.
